candidates.name: Haditha–Kirkuk Oil Pipeline (proposed connector)
candidates.sponsor: Chevron / Capital TI (US) / UCC Holding (Qatar) consortium (feasibility study only); Turkiye Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (proposal)

evidence.note: Iraq's cabinet cleared Basra Oil Company to sign preliminary agreements with a Chevron-led consortium to prepare technical/financial feasibility studies comparing the Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan and Basra-Haditha-Baniyas routes; studies due end-2026, construction start possibly 2027.

Names the consortium (Chevron, US-based Capital TI, Qatar's UCC Holding) and describes the routes as 'a pipeline from Basra that would split at Haditha ... before connecting to Syria, Turkey or Jordan,' and separately 'a pipeline from southern Iraq to Kirkuk in the north, with a second line leveraging existing infrastructure through Syria to the Mediterranean port of Baniyas' — i.e. the new build is the south-to-Kirkuk link; Kirkuk-Baniyas onward is existing/rehab infrastructure.

Confirms the Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan route name explicitly, connecting southern oil fields to Ceyhan 'via northern infrastructure,' and the separate Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route to the Syrian coast; both still exploratory with no financial/contractual obligations yet.

Confirms Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan route continues 'from Haditha through Kirkuk before reaching Ceyhan,' and separately notes the KBR consultancy contract is specifically for the Basra-Haditha segment (i.e. distinct from the Haditha-Kirkuk extension).

Describes Route 1 as starting at Basra, an intermediate point at Haditha, then 'extension: from Haditha to Kirkuk, then to Ceyhan in Turkey' — explicitly names the Haditha-Kirkuk leg as part of the studied corridor.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar (NTV interview, 18 Mar 2026): 'let us extend this pipeline, which currently runs up to Kirkuk, all the way to Basra' — independent corroboration of a Kirkuk-to-south-Iraq link (the same missing segment) proposed from the Turkish side, distinct from the Chevron-consortium study.

Turkiye aims to negotiate a comprehensive new agreement within one year that would 'extend the pipeline south from Kirkuk to the Basra Gulf region' and raise capacity to 2.5 million bpd, potentially adding an accompanying gas pipeline.

'Bayraktar has long advocated connecting Basra, Iraq's oil-rich southern region, to the north, where the Iraq-Turkey pipeline carries oil from Kirkuk to Turkey's Mediterranean port of Ceyhan' — confirms the missing link is the Basra/Haditha-to-Kirkuk connection, not the already-existing Kirkuk-Ceyhan leg itself.

candidates.why_maybe_new: The roster already has Basra->Haditha (P0544, construction) and Kirkuk->Ceyhan (P0547, operating) as separate, non-contiguous lines with no link between Haditha and Kirkuk. Every 2026 source (Chevron-led consortium's Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan/Basra-Haditha-Baniyas feasibility studies, and independently Turkiye's March 2026 proposal to extend Kirkuk-Ceyhan south) describes building or studying exactly that missing Haditha-Kirkuk (or Basra-Kirkuk) segment to tie the two existing systems together. This segment does not correspond to any existing PID — P0544 stops at Haditha, P5240 continues Haditha only toward Aqaba (not Kirkuk), and P0547/P1854/P2016 all start north at Kirkuk/Fish Khabur. Recommend as a new proposed-status row (or a monitor-note on P0544/P0547 if the consolidator prefers to treat it as a scope extension rather than a separate segment) pending outcome of the end-2026 feasibility studies.
